findings.title: Rule 16's operator action prescribes a re-drive of a terminally failed purge that no code path can perform
findings.arbiter_reasoning: markPurgeTerminalFailure (purge-stages.ts:1238-1248) writes status='failed', failed_step='purge' and never sets terminal_at. validatePurgeableOffboarding (purge-stages.ts:92-94) rejects any status other than 'purge_scheduled', so re-enqueuing the outbox row cannot resume - it re-enters validation, fails non-terminally, burns its retries and terminalizes again. AccountOffboardingPurgePoller (:103,:155) selects only 'purge_scheduled'. The one writer that can return a row to 'purge_scheduled', shouldTransitionToPurgeScheduled (provider-disposition.ts:281-282), refuses unless failed_step === 'teardown'. There is no admin retry route. The sentence also forbids the only two manual levers it names while naming no working one, and its terminal_at half describes a field this path never writes.

findings.title: The runbook doc-pin test pins the FILE, not the rule row: rule 16's fingerprint, tag filter and level can all be inverted and the test stays green
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured survivor RT-A6. Not an equivalent mutation: the mutant makes the documented rule route the retry issue and stay silent for the terminal one, which is the exact RT-08 failure this change exists to close. Not an unexecuted branch: the test reads the whole runbook at :850 and asserts on it. It survives only because expect(runbook).toContain('[account_offboarding_purge_failed, terminal]') is a file-wide substring check and the same string occurs at beta-launch-alerting.md:364 in the section-1 prose. The intake invariant 'the fingerprint values in the runbook row are byte-identical to the constants the worker sends; a test pins them' is therefore unenforced.

findings.title: The arch-review ledger asserts present-tense rule-1 coverage for a rule that is not configured and whose trigger is first-seen
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The ledger says the failed outbox row 'rides rule 1 as an aggregate count' and uses that to argue the ticket's premise was already half-closed. Rule 1 (health-alert -> discord) is unconfigured: its section-1 box at beta-launch-alerting.md:56 is unchecked. Its trigger is 'issue is first seen' (:449) and checks.ts:132 embeds the count in the title, so a repeat failure at the same count is not a new issue and does not re-fire - the same first-seen trap rule 16's own prose diagnoses. The runbook self-corrects in the same sentence; the durable ledger does not.
